# `verify_client`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Prove the client application by returning a signature over this socket's challenge.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, preprocessClientAuth @0x6b6bb0, set_cli_verified @0x6b5ff0 (64-bit imager build; key literal written to the public-key file there, modulus parsed as 1024 bits); 32-bit preprocessClientAuth @0x6814d8; app 3.3.2 VerifyAction and VerifyClientCmd |

Second step of client verification, after get_verify_str on the same socket. Matched by the authentication preprocessor before any method table, so it is answered on an unverified external connection. The client signs the challenge bytes and sends the base64 signature as sign together with the unchanged challenge as data. The device decodes sign and checks it over the exact data bytes with SHA-1 and an RSA public key compiled into the firmware (a 1024-bit modulus, READ; the 32-bit build carries the same key), and requires data to equal this socket's stored challenge. On success it sets the socket's verified flag and replies result 0, code 0. A failure does not clear an existing verified flag and an error reply does not by itself close the socket. The scheme authenticates the client application, not the user: the matching private signing key is held by the official app and is not part of this specification, so a client that cannot produce a valid signature cannot use an external connection (INFERRED). Internal (exact localhost-address) connections are treated as verified without this call. Only single requests get this dedicated reply; a batch from an unverified client is consumed silently. Ports with this preprocessor: 4700, 4701, 4702, 4400 and 4040. Verification on 4040 also gates the 4030 serial bridge by source IP (ports.md R3a).

Side effects: Normal path sets this socket's verified flag (connection-local) and writes scratch files for the verification utility. Omitting data selects a factory path that verifies hardware serial bytes and can set process-wide factory mode, which is why the tier is C.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"verify_client"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Signature over the challenge, and the challenge itself. Object form or positional [sign, data]. Extra object members and array elements beyond the second are ignored; with duplicate object members the first occurrence wins. Clients MUST send data (see verify_client). [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | sign or data present but not a string | `expected string param` |
| 207 | Signature does not verify, data does not match this socket's challenge, or no challenge was fetched on this socket | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Request has no id; reply has id null and no method member | `invalid id` |

Behaviour with params absent or of another JSON type is unresolved. The app requires code 0 and ends its session on any other code.

## Example

Request, request - sign and data are placeholders, not captured values:

```json
{"id":2,"method":"verify_client","params":{"sign":"c2lnbmF0dXJlLXBsYWNlaG9sZGVy","data":"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdef"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"verify_client","result":0,"code":0,"id":2}
```

Reply, bad-signature:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"verify_client","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":2}
```
